Incorporating the Beige Book, the outlook remains macro-positive but with measured caution. Multiple districts reported continued growth and job gains, with wage growth increasingly supplemented by nonwage benefits (health, profit-sharing, bonuses, paid vacation), reinforcing the FOMC’s view of a strong labor market. Household spending is supported by rising house prices in many markets. Price pressures vary across districts, and falling fuel prices temper headline inflation—consistent with inflation near 2 percent. Offsetting this, the SLOOS shows tighter lending standards for C&I and construction/land development and weaker demand for some CRE credit, implying headwinds for capex and CRE that align with the FOMC’s note of moderated business investment. Netting these, the Beige Book breadth nudges the stance slightly more positive than the initial read, but with downside risks still elevated relative to the statement alone.
